name: Otis Redding
hook: A Macon singer who started out copying Little Richard, got his chance at Stax as a driver for another act, wrote 'Respect', and died in a plane crash before his biggest hit came out.
blurb: Otis Redding was born in Dawson, Georgia, on 9 September 1941, the son of a sharecropper, and from age three grew up in Macon's Tindall Heights public housing project. He left school at 15 to support his family. His first hero was Little Richard, also from Macon: he worked with Richard's old backing band, the Upsetters, and won a local talent show singing Richard's 'Heebie Jeebies'. Sam Cooke was his other main model, especially 'Sam Cooke at the Copa'. In 1962 he drove the guitarist Johnny Jenkins to a recording session at Stax in Memphis. When it ended early, he was allowed to sing two songs. Jim Stewart thought the first sounded too much like Little Richard, but signed him on the strength of the ballad 'These Arms of Mine' (Volt, October 1962). Backed by Stax's house band, with Booker T. and the M.G.'s at its core, he became one of soul's greatest singers. 'Otis Blue' (1965) included his own song 'Respect', which Aretha Franklin later made her own, and a cover of the Rolling Stones' 'Satisfaction'. In June 1967 he played the Monterey Pop Festival, booked through Jerry Wexler, his first major show to a mostly white American audience. On 10 December 1967 his plane crashed into Lake Monona, near Madison, Wisconsin, and he died, aged 26. '(Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay', written with Steve Cropper and recorded days before, became the first record to reach number one on both the pop and R&B charts after its singer had died.
